content_html:
A fast, native database client for developers.
Free and open source.

Website · Docs · Download · Discord

Tiếng Việt 简体中文 한국어

About

TablePro is what I wanted TablePlus to be: native, fast, open source.

Built with native frameworks on every platform. No Electron, no JDBC, no JavaScript runtime. Connects to all major SQL and NoSQL databases through native drivers.

AI is built in: chat, inline suggestions, and an MCP server that lets Cursor, Raycast, or Claude Desktop talk to your databases. Bring your own API key, pick your own provider, or run local with Ollama.

Why TablePro

Native macOS database clients today fall into three groups:

  • Single-database, open source: Sequel Ace (MySQL only), Postico (PostgreSQL only). Great if you live in one engine.
  • Multi-database, closed source: TablePlus. Polished and native, but proprietary.
  • Multi-database, not native: DBeaver (JVM), Beekeeper Studio and DBGate (Electron). Cross-platform, but slow to start and heavy on memory.

TablePro is the missing fourth: native, multi-database, and open source.

Platforms

Platform Status
macOS 13+ Stable
iOS / iPadOS 18+ Stable
Linux (GNOME 50+) In development in linux/, not released yet
Windows No

Supported Databases

Built-in drivers ship with the app. Plugin drivers install on demand from the plugin registry. tablepro.app/databases has the current list and what each engine supports.

What's inside

  • SQL editor with autocomplete, multi-cursor, Vim mode, syntax themes
  • Data grid with inline editing, sort, filter, undo/redo
  • Native window tabs, multi-window, split panes
  • SSH tunnels with password and key authentication, SSL/TLS
  • Query history with full-text search
  • AI chat, inline suggestions, and Explain/Optimize
  • MCP server and URL scheme for Raycast, Cursor, Claude Desktop
  • Plugin system, write your own database driver in Swift

Free and paid

Everything above is free on every database, with no trial period or time limit. A license adds these to the Mac app:

Plan Adds
Starter iCloud Sync, Encrypted Export, Environment Variables, Linked Folders, Query Insights, Result Charts, Compare & Sync, Data Rewind
Team Everything in Starter, plus Team Catalog and Team Library

Plans and prices are on tablepro.app/pricing. The iPhone and iPad app needs no license.

Install

brew install --cask tablepro

Or download from GitHub Releases.

How to Build

These steps build the macOS and iOS apps; the Linux app builds with Meson and Cargo (linux/README.md).

Building TablePro requires Xcode 26 or later and XcodeGen.

The macOS and iOS apps live in apple/. Run the first-time setup, and every command below, from there:

brew install xcodegen
cd apple
scripts/download-libs.sh
scripts/generate-project.sh

TablePro.xcodeproj is generated from project.yml and is not in git. Re-run scripts/generate-project.sh after changing project.yml or Configs/, or after adding a source file.

Build a Debug app without code signing:

xcodebuild \
  -project TablePro.xcodeproj \
  -scheme TablePro \
  -configuration Debug \
  -skipPackagePluginValidation \
  CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO \
  build

The app is written to ~/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/TablePro-*/Build/Products/Debug/TablePro.app.

To build and run a signed app, put your Apple team and a unique bundle identifier in apple/Configs/Secrets.xcconfig. See Building with a personal Apple team.

Documentation

Full docs at docs.tablepro.app.

Support development

The app is free under AGPLv3. If you use TablePro at work, please buy a license. It adds the paid features, and every purchase funds the next release. If you can't afford one, just use the free version. That's why it's free.

Sponsors

Thanks to these amazing people for supporting TablePro:

SimpleLocalize · CodeRabbit · Nimbus · Dwarves Foundation

Contributors

Thanks to everyone who has contributed to TablePro:

Want to join them? Read CONTRIBUTING.md.
